title: geometry: move pure STL and OBJ mesh readers from app to camcraft-geometry

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Move the pure-Rust STL and OBJ mesh parsers from `camcraft-app` down into `camcraft-geometry`.

## Context
Research in #2593 found that `crates/app/src/geometry/import/stl.rs` and `crates/app/src/geometry/import/obj.rs` live in `camcraft-app`, although neither file uses Flecs, ECS, commands, or app types. `camcraft-sim` and `camcraft-simview` (#2586) depend on `camcraft-geometry` and must not depend on `camcraft-app` (#2574 answer 5). Moving these pure mesh readers to `camcraft-geometry` lets URDF loading read STL and OBJ meshes with zero new crate edges.

## Scope
- Move the pure STL parser (binary and ASCII, slice `parse` and streaming `parse_file`) and pure OBJ parser from `crates/app/src/geometry/import/` into `camcraft-geometry` (for example `crates/geometry/src/stl.rs` and `crates/geometry/src/obj.rs`).
- Keep the existing `MAX_FACETS`, `MAX_VERTICES`, finite-vertex checks, and non-degenerate-triangle checks intact.
- Keep `camcraft-geometry` free of Flecs, ECS, and new external dependencies.
- Re-export or wrap the moved readers in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/` so `load_model`, `parse_model`, `mesh_outward::turn_outward`, error types, and existing app callers behave identically.

## Done means
`camcraft-geometry` exposes public STL (binary and ASCII, slice and file) and OBJ parsers with the existing facet/vertex caps and degenerate-facet refusals, `camcraft-app` delegates to them with zero behaviour change, and both existing `app` import tests and new `camcraft-geometry` unit tests pass.

Part of #2593
